stories.headline: Oracle sends force majeure notice to Blue Owl over its 2.45GW Project Jupiter data center

key_facts.fact: Oracle sent a force majeure notice to the developer of Project Jupiter, a unit of Blue Owl Capital, seeking to delay payments if the New Mexico data center fails to come online in 2028 as planned, rather than walking away as main tenant.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than trying to walk away as the site's main tenant, Oracle is attempting to put off payments should the data center dubbed Project Jupiter get derailed and fail to come online in 2028 as planned

key_facts.fact: Oracle said 'Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule'; Blue Owl said the notice 'does not change the financial commitments to this multiyear project.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule," a spokesperson for Oracle said... "This notice does not change the financial commitments to this multiyear project," a Blue Owl spokesman said.

key_facts.fact: Debt tied to the development is already trading at stressed levels, below 90 cents on the dollar, according to a person familiar.
key_facts.excerpt: The debt tied to the development is already trading at stressed levels, below 90 cents on the dollar

key_facts.fact: The campus is designed for 2.45 GW and is part of the Stargate buildout for OpenAI; a key Energy Transfer gas pipeline meant to fuel it was delayed nearly six months to Feb. 1, 2027 after repeated permit denials by the New Mexico State Land Office.
key_facts.excerpt: the campus designed to handle 2.45 gigawatts... A key natural gas pipeline project developed by Energy Transfer LP that was supposed to begin service this month... was instead delayed by nearly six months to Feb. 1, 2027

key_facts.fact: Oracle shares fell 4% on Thursday after the report; Blue Owl shares also fell.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle shares fell 4% on Thursday following a report that the company sent a "force majeure" notice... Blue Owl Capital, which also saw its shares fall.

key_facts.fact: Project Jupiter is designed to be powered by gas-powered fuel cells from Bloom Energy.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Jupiter is designed to be powered by gas-powered fuel cells from Bloom Energy Corp.

stories.headline: Tower Semiconductor to make Japan its largest optical-chip hub, targeting 40x output by 2029

key_facts.fact: Tower Semiconductor CEO Russell Ellwanger told Nikkei on Thursday that the Israeli foundry will set up its largest production hub for optical communications chips in Japan under its planned $4 billion investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli foundry Tower Semiconductor will set up its largest production hub for optical communications semiconductors in Japan with its planned $4 billion investment, CEO Russell Ellwanger told Nikkei on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The investment is about $3 billion from Tower plus about $1 billion in Japanese government grants; Tower will convert its Arai fab to 300mm silicon photonics and advanced optical packaging and build a new 300mm fab next to Fab 7 in Uozu.
key_facts.excerpt: Tower is investing approximately $3 billion in its Japanese operations, backed by about $1 billion in grants from the Japanese government... convert its Arai facility... Tower will then build a new 300mm manufacturing facility next to Fab 7.

key_facts.fact: Tower has about $1.3 billion in contracted silicon photonics revenue for 2027, and customers have made about $290 million in prepayments to reserve capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Tower has contracts representing about $1.3 billion in Silicon Photonics revenue for 2027, while customers have already made about $290 million in prepayments to reserve capacity.

key_facts.fact: The expansion would let Tower produce the equivalent of 45,000 300mm wafers per month in 2029, roughly 40x its 2025 output, and the company will hire about 200 more workers; it also plans to bring co-packaged optics to Uozu.
key_facts.excerpt: produce the equivalent of 45,000 300mm wafers per month in 2029, an approximately 40x increase on production figures from 2025... hire around 200 additional workers... co-packaged optics

key_facts.fact: Tower first announced the Japan expansion plan, with METI support, in July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: July 14, 2026 – Tower Semiconductor... today announced a parallel dual-track strategic expansion of its 300mm Silicon Photonics (SiPho), Silicon Germanium (SiGe), and advanced packaging capabilities in Japan

stories.headline: Amazon to spend $100M+ on its fourth robot-making plant, in Indiana, doubling robot output

key_facts.fact: Amazon announced on Sept. 24 plans to invest more than $100 million in a 585,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana, creating 300 jobs, expected to launch by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon today announced plans to invest more than $100 million in a new 585,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility located in Greenwood, Indiana, creating 300 skilled manufacturing and engineering jobs... expected to launch by 2028.

key_facts.fact: The facility will produce products that power Amazon's fulfillment and robotics network, combining fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly; jobs average nearly $100,000 a year.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility will produce products that power Amazon's fulfillment and robotics network across North America... advanced fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating, and assembly

key_facts.fact: Amazon has manufactured more than one million robots in the US; they are deployed in more than 300 facilities and assist with 75% of all customer orders it delivers.
key_facts.excerpt: has manufactured more than one million robots in the U.S. to date. Those robots are now deployed across more than 300 facilities globally, assisting employees with 75% of all customer orders

key_facts.fact: Per the Wall Street Journal, it will be Amazon's fourth robot-making facility, and together with an Austin, Texas hub will double its robot-manufacturing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: The planned Indiana plant will be Amazon's fourth facility dedicated to producing robots... Together, the two new facilities in Indiana and Texas are set to double the e-commerce giant's total robot-manufacturing capacity.

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus expects $77M half-year loss ahead of its $5B Australian IPO

key_facts.fact: Australian data centre operator Firmus expects a pro forma loss after tax of $77 million for the first half of the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, according to two people citing a draft prospectus circulated this week.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus expects to report a loss after tax of $77 million for the first half of the financial year ending June 30, 2027, on a pro forma basis, the two people said, citing a draft prospectus circulated to prospective investors this week.

key_facts.fact: The draft prospectus contains no forecasts beyond that half and describes Firmus, founded in 2019, as historically loss-making.
key_facts.excerpt: The document did not contain any further forecasts beyond the first half of the 2027 financial year... described Firmus, founded in 2019, as historically loss-making

key_facts.fact: Firmus plans to raise A$7 billion (about $5 billion) with an institutional bookbuild starting Oct. 6, prospectus public Oct. 8, and ASX trading from Oct. 22.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus will launch its initial public offering to raise A$7 billion ($4.99 billion) to institutional investors on October 6... shares will start trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on October 22

key_facts.fact: It would be the second-largest IPO in Australia's history; Firmus has two operational data centres in Australia and Singapore and five under development in Asia-Pacific.
key_facts.excerpt: seeking to raise $7 billion in the second-largest IPO in Australia's history... Firmus has two operational data centres in Australia and Singapore. Five are under development across the Asia-Pacific.

key_facts.fact: Firmus started out mining Bitcoin and is backed by Nvidia and Blackstone; its valuation passed $10.5 billion by August.
key_facts.excerpt: By August the valuation had passed $10.5bn... it started out mining Bitcoin. Its backers now include Nvidia and Blackstone

stories.headline: Google to launch first TPU satellite on Oct. 1, testing AI data centers in orbit

key_facts.fact: Google said on Sept. 24 it will launch a prototype satellite carrying its Tensor Processing Units on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare, the first in-orbit test of Project Suncatcher; the satellite was developed with Planet.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Suncatcher is scheduled to embark on its first test in orbit, launching a prototype satellite to evaluate how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space... Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX was developed in partnership with Planet.

key_facts.fact: The fridge-sized satellite, called MVP, carries four TPUs, launches October 1 on a Falcon 9, and its solar panels provide about one kilowatt of power.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellite, dubbed MVP, is about the size of a refrigerator. Inside, it has four of Google's custom TPU AI accelerators... solar panels... about one kilowatt of power

key_facts.fact: Google will run Gemini models on the TPUs, but the cooling system only allows about 15 minutes of operation before the chips must shut down.
key_facts.excerpt: Google will run Gemini models on the TPUs, but they won't be able to run continuously. The cooling system will only be able to operate in brief spurts of about 15 minutes.

key_facts.fact: In proton-beam tests at UC Davis, Google's Trillium TPUs survived a radiation dose greater than a five-year space mission would deliver.
key_facts.excerpt: Initial results have shown that our Trillium TPUs hold up remarkably well, and can survive a radiation total ionizing dose greater than what they would receive during a five-year space mission.

key_facts.fact: Google plans to put two satellites in orbit in 2027 to test laser links between TPU-carrying satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: Google plans to put two satellites into orbit next year.

stories.headline: TSMC to raise wafer prices 3-6% from January 2027, with orders booked to 2030

key_facts.fact: TSMC will raise wafer prices by about 3% to 6% starting January 2027, with the biggest increases for advanced nodes such as 2nm and 3nm, Digitimes reported on Wednesday citing supply chain sources; TSMC did not comment.
key_facts.excerpt: According to unnamed sources cited by DigiTimes, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSMC plans to raise its wafer prices by approximately 3% to 6%, effective January 2027. The increase is expected to be more pronounced for advanced manufacturing processes. TSMC has not commented

key_facts.fact: TSMC's 8-inch fabs run at over 100% utilization, nodes below 45nm are fully loaded, and some order visibility extends through 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Currently, TSMC's 8-inch fabs are running at over 100% utilization and nodes below 45nm are fully loaded. Order visibility has already extended through 2030.

key_facts.fact: Orders beyond pre-committed volumes for AI/HPC chips carry a separate 10-15% surcharge on top of the base increase.
key_facts.excerpt: For customers placing orders beyond their pre-committed volumes — the overflow AI chip orders that Nvidia, AMD, and Google consistently need as demand spikes — a separate surcharge of 10 to 15 percent sits on top

key_facts.fact: The 3-6% figure came in below Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan's projection; TSMC's US-listed shares closed about 1.2% lower Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan had projected TSMC could raise leading-edge wafer prices by 5 to 10 percent in 2027... TSMC shares listed in New York closed about 1.2 percent lower Wednesday

stories.headline: Qualcomm renews its global patent license with Apple from April 2027

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm announced on Sept. 24 the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm Incorporated today announced the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm licensing chief John Han said: 'We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement.' No term length or financial details were disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement," said John Han... There are no details yet about how long the license pact is for.

key_facts.fact: The previous deal came from an April 2019 settlement ending a two-year global legal battle: a six-year license from April 1, 2019, with a two-year extension option that expires at the end of March 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the settlement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm, the companies dropped litigation worldwide and agreed to a six-year global patent licensing deal from April 1, 2019. The agreement gave Apple an option to extend the license by two years.
